entrypoints.summary: GET /file accepts filename, ct, and q; it selects a known template, validates a text/* Content-Type, replaces TEMPLATE_QUERY_JS with JsEncode(q), and returns the response using the supplied content type.
The official payload targets /file?filename=script.js with ct=text/html;charset=x-Chinese-CNS and an attacker-controlled q value.

affected_components.role: Accepts request-selected response content type, applies category-based JavaScript encoding to q, and inserts it in the JavaScript template.
Places the flag in same-origin localStorage and visits the supplied localhost URL.

code_slices.surrounding_context: Code pages are registered globally. The JavaScript template embeds the reflected query in a single-quoted assignment, while the bot establishes the privileged same-origin storage condition.
code_slices.vulnerable: The /file handler validates only that ct begins with text/, uses it in Results.Text, and replaces TEMPLATE_QUERY_JS with JsEncode(q). JsEncode emits Unicode letters and whitespace directly while escaping other characters.

negative_controls: No supplied artifact records a successful exfiltration request or a completed exploit run.
The bot rejects URLs not beginning with http://localhost:1337/.
observability.positive_marker: The bot makes the flag available in localStorage at the localhost origin that executes the injected script.

preconditions: The service is running in the supplied .NET 8.0 and Chrome 136.0.7103.94 environment.
A bot visit is made to an http://localhost:1337/ URL.
The browser follows the writeup's documented fallback behavior for the unsupported X-Chinese-CNS charset.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A /file URL with filename=script.js, X-Chinese-CNS charset, and a q payload built from mapped Unicode characters plus JavaScript grammar.
trigger_steps.summary: Request script.js from /file with ct=text/html;charset=x-Chinese-CNS and the documented q value containing selected Unicode characters whose X-Chinese-CNS sequences include JavaScript punctuation bytes.

impact.security_effect: Same-origin script execution in the privileged bot's localhost page context.

causal_trace.summary: The attacker controls q and can supply a syntactically accepted text/* Content-Type with a charset for the /file response.

JsEncode preserves Unicode letters and whitespace but Unicode-escapes other characters; after legacy code pages are registered, selected permitted letters can be encoded by .NET in X-Chinese-CNS multibyte sequences containing ASCII punctuation bytes.

For the documented unsupported X-Chinese-CNS declaration, Chromium defaults to windows-1252 and interprets the emitted multibyte trailing bytes as single-byte JavaScript punctuation, including a quote that can terminate the reflected single-quoted string.

The documented payload uses the resulting JavaScript grammar to execute attacker-controlled script in the localhost origin visited by the bot; that origin has a flag stored in localStorage before navigation.

failure.operation: Browser fallback decoding of server-emitted X-Chinese-CNS bytes transforms a byte within an allowed Unicode character's encoding into JavaScript punctuation in the reflected script.

primary_invariant.statement: Characters accepted and escaped for insertion into the JavaScript string must be serialized and decoded by the browser so that they cannot become unescaped JavaScript delimiters or operators.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The server's Unicode-category decision is made before it serializes allowed letters through an attacker-selected legacy charset, whereas Chromium's documented fallback reads selected multibyte bytes as windows-1252 single-byte characters.

quality.review_notes: Primary source and official writeup support the encode/decode differential and a concrete payload. The documented browser behavior is runtime-specific to Chromium and the supplied environment pins Chrome 136. No patch, observed exploit run, or independently recorded flag exfiltration event is present; mitigation is invariant-derived rather than an implemented remediation.

remediation.invariant_restored: Emit the reflected script using a fixed browser-supported encoding and server-controlled content type so the browser decodes the same canonical representation on which validation and escaping operate.
mitigation_classes: contextual JavaScript escaping under canonical encoding

target.component: ASP.NET `/file` response generation and reflected JavaScript template
target.project_or_package: Google CTF 2025 Quals Lost In Transliteration challenge

oracle.expected_negative: With a fixed browser-supported encoding and non-attacker-controlled response charset, permitted Unicode letters do not undergo fallback byte reinterpretation into JavaScript punctuation.
oracle.expected_positive: A documented /file URL using the X-Chinese-CNS charset and q payload produces a script response whose browser-decoded JavaScript escapes the intended string context and can execute in the localhost origin.
